label: Late-episode (t>=92) D2 after rewarded a2->S2 then a2->S2 again, scaled by S2 belief
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 0.4% of steps, ~0.2-0.36 when on) that is zero at D1 and GO. It fires only at D2 in the last ~8 trials of the episode, when the previous trial was a rewarded a2->S2 (prev a2/S2 unknown at window start also allowed) and this trial again chose a2 and reached S2 (common). Magnitude rises with episode trial (near zero before ~92, partial at 92-93, full from ~94) and with the ideal observer confidence that S2 is good (-belief_lo). All terms are observed at D2 (this trial choice and state are shown at D2), so no future variables. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.57, test 0.53; the profile additive ceilings are tiny (all 0.05, all observed 0.03) because the feature needs a conjunction. Single conjunction indicator with ep>=90 gives 0.35 dev; adding belief and a finer late-episode ramp brings it to 0.57. A streak term (trial -2 also a2->S2 rewarded) and the trial-before reward did not help. Remaining error: all-or-none firing, some qualifying trials at t90-93 fire fully and some at t95+ stay silent, not captured by observed history in the window.

issues: Scores reproduce: the claimed terms get R^2 beyond timing 0.573 on dev and 0.528 on test. The profile's additive ceilings are 0.05 (all) and 0.03 (all observed), so the claim that this is a conjunction feature holds. The profile residuals are exactly 0 at D1 and GO, and at D2 only the 'after a2 S2 r' cell is positive (+0.0075).

The ramp is described a little too simply. Per-trial indicators for the conjunction with a known previous a2->S2 rewarded trial, measured on top of the D2 decile-9 baseline of about 0.03, give roughly +0 for t<88, -0.018 at t90, +0.04 at t92, +0.10 at t93, +0.14 at t94, +0.175 at t95, then +0.20 / +0.21 / +0.18 / +0.15 at t96-99. So the effect peaks at t96-97 and falls back at t98-99. It is not 'full from ~94'.

'Fires only in the last ~8 trials' is true on average but not per window. In misses, windows that start at t90 or t91 with a run of rewarded a2->S2c trials fire fully (0.28-0.32) from t90 on, where the model predicts 0.03. These are the top systematic misses. Belief, belief_cover and window position do not explain them: split terms for t89-93 x (belief_lo<=-3), (trial==0) and belief_cover get weights of about 0.00-0.03. So the all-or-none leftover the explainer admits to is real and cannot be explained from observed quantities.

The belief effect works more like a threshold than the claimed linear clip(-belief_lo). Conjunction x ramp by belief bin: belief_lo>0 gives 0.04, (0,-3] about 0.09-0.12, and <=-3 gives 0.21 (no rows below -4). Using the threshold version: dev 0.581 vs 0.576.

The claim that a streak term did not help is only partly true. Requiring that no a1 choice appears at trials -2..-4 of the window gets weight +0.09 and raises dev R^2 from 0.531 to 0.543; tv('action',-2)==1 alone gets weight -0.15. The gains are small, but earlier window history does matter somewhat.

My better terms add only about 0.05 on test (0.577 vs 0.528). No large systematic error class is left that observed variables can explain. The leftover over-prediction is spread across D2 cells after other previous-trial patterns, each around -0.003, which is small.

skeptic.better_terms: C = (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action != 1) * (prev_state != 1) * (action == 2) * (state == 2); R = np.clip((ep_trial-91)/4,0,1); terms: C*R ;; C*R*(belief_lo<=-3) ;; C*R*(tv('action',-2)!=1)*(tv('action',-3)!=1)*(tv('action',-4)!=1) ;; C*R*(tv('reward',-2)!=0)*(tv('reward',-3)!=0)*(tv('reward',-4)!=0) ;; C*R*(ep_trial>=98) ;; C*R*belief_cover
